kill_fact: No kill fact found. I attacked all four vectors against primary sources and the bear case survived every one. (a) COST-CURVE: the record's cost claim verifies against the company's own Q2 2026 disclosure - total cash costs $1,054/oz and all-in sustaining cost ~$1,459/oz, both inside the 2026 guidance ranges ($1,020-1,120 and $1,400-1,550) and, per management on the 2026-07-30 call, BELOW first-quarter costs and below the guidance midpoints. If anything the record's 'unit costs rose' framing is softer than the primary text supports; the genuine forward cost risk is narrower and dated - the CFO confirmed on that same call, in answer to Barclays, that Canadian Malartic cash-cost guidance was raised for the second half of 2026. (b) RESERVE/CONTRACT: no undisclosed downgrade found; the reserve figures are not load-bearing for the bear side and no bear number depends on them. (c) CYCLICAL-PEAK: this is the one place the record could have been trapped and it is not - the valuation guard FAILS (base fair value below the market price), and the peak-cycle denominator makes the bear's central claim stronger, not weaker: the 8.6x trailing EV/EBITDA is struck on twelve months of EBITDA earned at realised gold well above the $4,200/oz base deck, so the forward multiple on the record's own deck is roughly 9.0x. (d) HIDDEN DISQUALIFIER: none. No reserve downgrade, no permit or licence action, no equity dilution funding capex (diluted share count fell year on year and the company repurchased stock every quarter), and no streaming or royalty structure of any kind - Agnico is a royalty BUYER (the $5M Prism net-profit-interest buy-back, 2026-06-04), not a seller. The junior-equity book (C$22.4M Wallbridge 2026-05-20, C$60.0M Cadillac 2026-07-24) is real and confirmed by primary releases, but at ~1% of market value it is a governance flag, not a disqualifier. What does move is the base-case level: the record's own sum-of-the-parts does not tie to its stated total, and the share count is stale post-Rupert.
corrections: 1) BASE FAIR VALUE, $164 -> $161 (the one number that moved). The record's own base-case parts are $69.2B producing mines + $8.0B growth pipeline + $3.27B net cash + $1.2B junior equity = $81.67B, not the '$82.5B' stated, and the per-share components it lists ($138 + $16 + $6.50 + $2.40) sum to $162.90, not $164. Separately the divisor is stale: the record uses 503M diluted shares, which is the Q2 2026 weighted-average (502.9M) and therefore captures only two weeks of the shares issued to close the Rupert Resources arrangement on 2026-06-16. Actual shares outstanding as of 2026-08-11 are ~506.4M ($91.903B market cap / $181.495). $81.67B / 506.4M = $161.3. The correction is fully within the bear's direction - it widens the gap to the $181.44 price from 10.6% to 12.7% - so nothing in the conclusion turns on it. 2) NET CASH, footnote only, not carried into the level. The record's $3.27B follows management's own definition (the CEO said 'approximately $3.3 billion' on the 2026-07-30 call), but the filed balance sheet also carries $34.3M of short-term debt and $89.1M of finance leases against $3,473.7M of cash and short-term investments, i.e. $3.15B on a strict basis. Using $3.15B leaves the corrected fair value at $161 either way, so the level is robust to the choice. 3) SOP_BEAR HEADER MISLABEL, footnote. The adverse case is headed 'about $107 a share (roughly $54B of equity value)', but the four parts listed underneath sum to $50.3B, which is $99-100 a share. The $54B is a back-solve from the point number, not the sum of the parts. The $107 itself is defensible and I am NOT correcting it: the record discloses that it blends the sum-of-the-parts with the commodity-beta cross-check, and the two legs check out independently - $50.3B / 506.4M = $99.3, and 1.55 beta x 23.5% gold decline = 36.4% off $181.44 = $115.4; the midpoint is $107.4. The header wording should say so rather than attributing $54B to the parts. 4) MULTIPLE-REVERSION ARITHMETIC OVERSTATED, footnote. 'A reversion merely to Newmont's 8.2 times... costs about 5%' - at 8.2x on $10.36B TTM EBITDA plus net cash the price is $175.4, a 3.3% fall, not 5%. 'A reversion to the 6.8-7.8 times where AngloGold and Alamos trade costs 15-25%' - that band actually maps to $146.5-$167.2, a fall of 8% to 19%, not 15-25%; and the closing claim that the 6.8-8.2x band 'alone takes the stock to the low $150s' corresponds to ~7.1x, near the bottom of the band rather than its middle ($161 at the midpoint). The direction is right and the peer ranking is exactly right; the magnitudes at the shallow end are overstated.
